title: Synthesis and Tribological Characteristics of High-Performance Self-Lubricating CoCrFeNiMo<sub>x</sub>-Ni/MoS<sub>2</sub>-Ag-Cr<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> Composites.

recollection.starting_material: Guess: Gas-atomized CoCrFeNiMo_x high-entropy alloy (HEA) powders as the matrix, combined with Ni-coated MoS2 (Ni/MoS2) solid lubricant particles, Ag powder, and Cr2O3 ceramic powder. The Mo content x in the HEA was varied to tune matrix hardness/phase constitution.
recollection.intervention: Guess: Powder blending (e.g., ball milling) of HEA with Ni/MoS2, Ag, and Cr2O3, followed by pressure-assisted densification such as spark plasma sintering or hot pressing to near-full density. The Ni coating on MoS2 was used to improve thermal stability and interfacial bonding during sintering. Post-process involved tribological testing from room temperature to elevated temperatures.
recollection.structure: Guess: A dense composite with an FCC CoCrFeNi-based matrix where increasing Mo (x) promotes precipitation (e.g., sigma/μ/B2) that strengthens the matrix; uniformly dispersed Cr2O3 hard particles and Ag soft phases; retained Ni/MoS2 lubricant particulates. During sliding, a tribofilm forms composed of MoS2/Ag at room temperature and oxidized species (e.g., Ag2MoO4, NiMoO4, MoO3) with Cr2O3 enrichment at elevated temperatures.
recollection.mechanism: Guess: At room temperature, shear of layered MoS2 and plasticity/flow of Ag provide low shear strength at the interface, while the HEA matrix and Cr2O3 confer load support and wear resistance. The Ni shell stabilizes MoS2 during sintering and improves adhesion and chemical compatibility, helping to retain lubricant in the matrix. At elevated temperatures, partial oxidation of MoS2 to MoO3 and reaction with Ag/Ni yields lubricious oxides (e.g., Ag2MoO4, NiMoO4), sustaining a continuous, low-shear tribofilm; Cr2O3 remains as a stable, hard phase that supports the contact and reduces abrasive wear. The Mo-enriched HEA matrix resists softening and contributes to toughness, limiting delamination.
recollection.results: Guess: An optimized composition (intermediate Mo content x and balanced Ni/MoS2–Ag–Cr2O3) achieved a friction coefficient around 0.08–0.12 at room temperature with wear rates on the order of 10^-6–10^-5 mm^3/N·m. At elevated temperatures (e.g., 400–600 °C), friction remained below ~0.25–0.30 with low wear due to formation of Ag–Mo–O tribofilms. The composite reached near-full density (>98%), exhibited increased hardness (approximately 6–8 GPa depending on x), and showed improved wear resistance compared to HEA-only or single-lubricant controls.

score.note: The recollection correctly identifies powder blending/SPS processing, variation of Mo content, an FCC matrix with Mo-promoted sigma-type precipitation, and temperature-dependent MoS2/Ag and silver-molybdate tribofilms. Its lubrication and strengthening mechanisms are substantially correct, though several details are speculative or unsupported, such as NiMoO4, uniform Cr2O3 dispersion, and the claimed role of the Ni shell. Quantitative recall is weak: the 0.25–0.30 elevated-temperature friction range is near the reported 0.23–0.26 minimum values, but the stated temperature range is wrong, room-temperature friction is unsupported, hardness is too high, and the generic wear-rate range misses the very high 400 °C values.
